item.title: Allahabad HC cites long trial, lets off offenders, SC slams ‘misplaced sympathy’
item.description: A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said it was a case of misplaced sympathy. The trial court had awarded fiveyear jail terms to the two, but the HC released them on probation. SC said the case was “doomed from its inception insofar as justice delivery to the victim is concerned”.
item.dc:creator: AMIT ANAND CHOUDHARY

item.title: 'Russia a big machine': Trump says Ukraine 'has to want' to settle war with Putin
item.description: US president Trump pointed to Russia's ability to sustain its military campaign and capture territory, portraying Moscow as having the upper hand in the conflict. "Russia is a big machine - they just keep grinding forward, and that's what they've done. They've taken a very large piece of land," he said.
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV SINGH

item.title: Identify, defeat forces against India: Modi calls for unity, self-reliance
item.description: PM urges parties, institutions to put nation first; says national self-respect and strength key to overcoming challenges
item.dc:creator: MANASH PRATIM GOHAIN

item.title: In talks with Reliance to refine more Venezuelan oil: Marco Rubio
item.description: US secretary of state Marco Rubio is visiting Jamnagar Wednesday to tour the Reliance refinery and, in a lastminute change of schedule, is likely to spend the night there. He was earlier scheduled to leave around 9pm and return to Mumbai. In Jamnagar, he will have dinner with Mukesh Ambani at the Vantara centre. Rubio’s visit to Jamnagar comes within weeks of a vicious attack on Ambani by Elon Musk.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Police lens on Lawrence Bishnoi’s aide Randeep Malik in Tiger Shroff shooting case
item.description: Anil Pandit Pandit and Shroff ’s shooter Rehan both reported to Malik and were considered “his men” till a few months ago, a source said. Rehan had been earlier tasked by Malik and Pandit with a shooting incident in Sonipat as well. “Rehan was shown the same ‘American dream’ that Malik had shown Pandit in the past,” a source said.
item.dc:creator: RAJ SHEKHAR JHA

item.title: Jensen Huang and his wife donated $75 million to Vanderbilt
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: 2 British Indians assaulted during Dussehra, Bathukamma celebrations
item.description: The assaults happened on Oct 17 outside Ossett Town Hall, which was hosting the celebration. The event was organised by local Telugu Hindu community groups. Earlier in the evening a group of around 25 local white youths, mostly male, were cycling around on e-bikes asking organisers what was going on in the town hall and who was inside.
item.dc:creator: NAOMI CANTON

item.title: Florida couple missed 66 mortgage payments; man's bank lawsuit rejected
item.description: A Florida couple missed 66 monthly mortgage payments on their Naples property, triggering a foreclosure dispute that began in 2009. During the legal battle, Gregory Brian Myers agreed to deposit $5,000 monthly while appealing the foreclosure. He later sued U.S. Bank, alleging it had violated their agreement. On October 19, 2026, a federal appeals court upheld the dismissal of his lawsuit.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Hacker group claims access to 3.8 lakh SBI data entries
item.description: The claim was highlighted by cybersecurity monitoring account CyberPulse56 in a post on social media platform X. According to the account, the group purportedly possesses about 3.8 lakh data entries in CSV format and 2,722 pdf documents associated with the country’s largest public sector lender. The allegedly exposed dataset is said to contain customers’ personal information, residential addresses, loan applications, supporting documents and other applicationrelated records.
item.dc:creator: Agencies

item.title: Desi Bela Bajaria leaves Netflix after giving global blockbusters
item.description: Bela Bajaria has stepped down from her role as chief content officer at Netflix amid significant challenges in the media landscape. She oversaw an impressive annual budget of almost $20 billion while bolstering Netflix's international content strategy. With a decline in audience engagement highlighting the industry's evolution, the streaming giant is poised for a transformative approach. Peter Rice, formerly of Disney and Fox, is set to take the helm.
item.dc:creator: CHIDANAND RAJGHATTA

item.title: Valentino-built Hollywood villa bought for $1.05m later sold for $2.5m
item.description: The Hollywood home at 6823 Iris Circle sold for $2.5 million, exceeding its asking price by $205,000. Initially bought for $1.05 million in 2016, the house underwent extensive renovations highlighting its history and charm. The property, linked to Rudolph Valentino and Pola Negri, boasts original features alongside modern updates. Located in Whitley Heights, a historic district, the neighborhood is known for its celebrity inhabitants.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: Tamera Mowry lists home for $2.69m after buying 15-acre Napa estate for $3.8m
item.description: Tamera Mowry-Housley and Adam Housley are making waves in real estate as they list their picturesque Fairfield, California home for $2.69 million. Having acquired a quaint Napa Valley estate that requires renovations, their vision focuses on sustainable living with an orchard and vineyard to nurture their children's outdoor adventures. This shift marks a profound transformation in their family lifestyle, moving from spacious interiors to embracing more land and nature.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: US govt bans American tech firm from Green Card programme for 2 yrs; fines $1.4 mn
item.description: Cloudera, a data management company, has been banned from the Permanent Labor Certification program for two years. This decision follows allegations of discrimination against qualified U.S. workers during its recruitment process. A fine of $1.4 million will be imposed to resolve the case and compensate affected workers. Additionally, the company will face compliance obligations to uphold federal labor laws. This settlement highlights ongoing efforts to protect U.S.
item.dc:creator: TOI TECH DESK

item.title: Texas family backed 204-acre park plan on ranchland sought for 3,500 homes
item.description: In June 2016, San Antonio city officials approved the acquisition of 204 acres of the Classen-Steubing Ranch. This initiative aims to preserve the land essential for the Edwards Aquifer recharge zone. The planned park space balances conservation with recreational facilities like sports fields and trails. Acquisition funding primarily derives from Texas's voter-approved Edwards Aquifer protection program and city budgets.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: Delhi HC cites national security, junks CIC order to IAF on PMs’ foreign trips
item.description: Allowing a petition by the Central Public Information Officer of Directorate of Personal Services, Air Headquarters, Justice Amit Mahajan held the IAF was justified in denying access to the records under section 8 of RTI that exempts disclosure of information that could jeopardise national security or pose a risk to a person’s life and physical safety.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Smartphone shipments slip, Chinese brands lose ground
item.description: Vivo’s shipments dropped 34% to 6.4 million — the sharpest decline among the top five. Repeated price increases disrupted retailers’ inventory planning, while limited supplies of entry-level phones weakened its position. Xiaomi’s traditional appeal of offering more features for the money also came under pressure. Rising component costs forced trade-offs on pricing and memory configurations, with shipments falling 28% to 4.7 million.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: Travis Kelce’s $5.35M mansion faces another property review
item.description: Travis Kelce’s $5.35 million Ohio mansion faces fresh scrutiny as local officials continue reviewing plans for the historic lakeside estate. While the revised six-foot privacy fence received approval in September, the proposed rear landscaping remains unresolved. Neighbors have raised concerns about tree heights and potential damage to shared sewer lines. Bratenahl’s Architectural Review Board is scheduled to revisit the landscaping proposal on November 10, 2026, leaving parts of the property improvements pending.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Maria Sharapova’s $25M mansion sale: How did her $4.1M lot become a record deal?
item.description: Maria Sharapova bought a Manhattan Beach lot for $4.1 million in 2012 and built a three-story home with Japanese-inspired design. In 2025, NBA star Luka Dončić bought the property for $25 million, setting a local residential sale record. The deal marked a major rise in the home’s reported value, although Sharapova’s final profit remains unknown.
item.dc:creator: GLOBAL SPORTS DESK

item.title: Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman warns of unrest bid by ‘2 united parties’
item.description: PM said attempts were made to create labour unrest at some factories in different parts of the country, adding that intelligence reports indicated that the ousted authoritarian regime was supplying money for such activities. “There is a party also here that spreads rumours in the country. The party tried to sell various tickets to the people before the election by telling lies. These two parties have now united,” he said.
item.dc:creator: AHSAN TASNIM

item.title: India, US ‘perfectly aligned’ on key issues: Rubio; defends ties with Pakistan
item.description: Addressing a gathering of India Inc’s leading business figures, Rubio said the relationship between the two countries could help shape the future of the global economy, particularly as advances in artificial intelligence and quantum computing transform industries and societies. “I truly believe the relationship between US and India is defining, in many ways, in a positive way, what the 21st century can look like,” he said.
item.dc:creator: TNN

item.title: India & US to boost defence, energy ties, Marco Rubio says trade deal close
item.description: Rubio’s second visit to India comes against the backdrop of the US’s Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act, which is intended to penalise countries purchasing Russian oil, and Trump’s subsequent temporary suspension of related tariffs. India maintains that its oil procurement is essential not only for its own energy security but also for the stability of global markets. Rubio lauded the “substantial progress” made by India in diversifying its energy portfolio.
item.dc:creator: SACHIN PARASHAR

item.title: No double standards on terror, need unified action to dismantle its entire ecosystem: Rajnath at SCO; says members will have to work together on resilient supply chains
item.description: During the SCO meeting in Dushanbe, Rajnath Singh emphasised the need for collective efforts against terrorism. He stated that terrorism undermines investments while calling for an end to double standards. Furthermore, he discussed India's initiatives to enhance connectivity and trade with Central Asia for mutual development. Rajnath highlighted India's significant contribution to global economic growth amidst a worldwide slowdown.
item.dc:creator: SURENDRA SINGH

item.title: Harry Warner's Beverly Hills mansion listed for nearly $40m, sold for $27.25m
item.description: A legendary mansion in Beverly Hills, originally built for Harry Warner, has changed hands for $27.25 million after an extended listing. Initially priced at nearly $40 million in 2016, the estate received extensive upgrades while maintaining its Old Hollywood charm. Featuring a guesthouse linked to Marilyn Monroe, this property has hosted myriad celebrations.
item.dc:creator: TOI REAL ESTATE DESK

item.title: Tiger Shroff firing case: Delhi Police arrests 4 accused, including 2 women
item.description: In a significant breakthrough, the Delhi Police Special Cell has detained four suspects—Kunal, Sumit, Radha, and Babita—as part of an ongoing probe. These individuals have been transferred to the Mumbai Police, who are seeking a transit remand to delve deeper into a shooting incident linked to actor Tiger Shroff's vehicle. Previously, three other suspects were arrested in Rajasthan and have since been brought to Mumbai for interrogation.
item.dc:creator: ANJALI SINGH

item.title: Trump’s tariff waiver on Russian oil: India gets relief for now, but is it credible?
item.description: For India, the immediate relief is for its crude supply basket and exporters. If India decided to give up Russian crude oil, its single largest supplier would have gone off the table, with no easy replacement amid Middle East tensions. If it continued to buy Russian crude, then the 100% tariffs would have weighed on its exports to the US.
item.dc:creator: SMRITI JAIN

item.title: Delhi BJP leader burns cockroach effigy; Dipke responds with SRK’s 'Swades' song
item.description: During Dussehra celebrations in Delhi, a 30-foot cockroach effigy was burned alongside traditional effigies of Ravan. Organizers stated that the effigy symbolized filth and promoted cleanliness in line with health awareness initiatives. Leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party reacted sharply, suggesting the move provided them with free publicity. Delhi minister Kapil Mishra remarked that cockroaches symbolize chaos and filth, reflecting public sentiment.
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: Harmanpreet Kaur’s 91 powers India to 3-0 T20I series sweep against Zimbabwe
item.description: India's women's cricket team displayed sheer dominance against Zimbabwe, clinching the third T20I by a commanding 92 runs. With Shafali Verma and Harmanpreet Kaur leading the charge, scoring 69 and 91 respectively, Zimbabwe struggled in the chase, ending at 124/7 after facing early setbacks. Nandani Sharma's stellar three-wicket performance solidified the win, marking an impressive 11-match T20I winning streak.
item.dc:creator: NITESH DUBEY

item.title: K3G lessons, cricket, no spice: How is Prince William preparing to come to India
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: 'Enough drama': Prince Harry says he wants to reconcile with family after years of rift
item.description: Prince Harry recently opened up about the need for reconciliation with his family, sharing his personal experiences that resonate with many who struggle with familial conflicts. He conveyed his aspirations for nurturing better connections with his father, King Charles III, and brother, Prince William. Harry also reflected on the joyous moments of his children attending a British school, honoring his mother's legacy and embracing a new chapter of healing.
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN

item.title: Shinde calls INDIA bloc ‘ten-headed Ravana’, accuses Uddhav of ‘vote theft’
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: California's 750-acre Irvine Lake to be drained for five-year dam repairs
item.description: This month, Irvine Lake will see a significant decrease in water levels as vital dam repairs begin. The planned drawdown will facilitate crucial construction activities, enhancing the dam's structural integrity as per regulatory requirements. Water managers are closely monitoring potential winter weather effects to ensure community safety, while conversations with environmental specialists are underway to safely relocate fish and address concerns from anglers.
item.dc:creator: TOI WORLD DESK

item.title: AAP demands FIR over 30ft cockroach effigy burned alongside Ravan in Delhi
item.description: AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj lodged a complaint against the Shri Keshav Ramlila Committee for burning a cockroach effigy. He claimed the act hurt religious sentiments and demanded the registration of an FIR against the organisers. Delhi minister Kapil Mishra, who attended the event, responded sarcastically to the complaint. The effigy was burned alongside traditional figures of Ravan, Kumbhakaran, and Meghnad during the event.
item.dc:creator: SIDDHI DHARMADHIKARI

item.title: 'Where are the fans?' Warner calls out lack of fans at South Africa-Australia Tests
item.description: David Warner is voicing alarm over the dismal attendance during the ongoing Test series between South Africa and Australia. Both teams hold the top two positions in Test cricket rankings, yet crowds have been sparse. Rain has exacerbated the situation, resulting in noticeably empty stands. With the echoes of the 2018 ball-tampering scandal lingering, this series' low turnout raises critical questions about the future of Test cricket's allure.
item.dc:creator: NITESH DUBEY

item.title: Memo from New Delhi: Make America India Again?
item.description: Donald Trump proposed renaming New Mexico to New America, claiming it would enhance pride among residents and change election integrity. Political representatives from New Mexico opposed the idea, emphasizing the state's historical significance and established name. Constitutional barriers exist, as name changes require formal processes involving local and national laws. Historical context surrounding America’s naming is complex and reflects a mix of cultural influences.
item.dc:creator: CHIDANAND RAJGHATTA

item.title: Tiger Shroff wasn’t original target, shooters switched due to tight security: Cops
item.description: Mumbai Crime Branch revealed Tiger Shroff was not the shooters' intended target as they aimed for another celebrity. Due to tight security around the intended target, the shooters shifted focus to Shroff instead. The suspects were arrested in Rajasthan's Kota and granted a 48-hour transit remand for transport to Mumbai. Following the remand, the Mumbai Police adopted an alternative strategy for the safety of the accused.
item.dc:creator: SIDDHI DHARMADHIKARI

item.title: 'Disregards consensus': China slams US for after DeepSeek ban from govt IT systems
item.description: China has strongly criticized the US for its recent ban on the DeepSeek AI model, claiming it undermines the interests of Chinese enterprises. The Chinese commerce ministry pointed out that the US Department of Homeland Security's concerns regarding security threats from DeepSeek products are unfounded. China warns against the politicization of technology and national security concerns, suggesting that this development could further strain economic relations between the two superpowers.
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN

item.title: 'Youth on streets are revolutionaries': Uddhav Thackeray calls for 'regime change'
item.description: During the vibrant Dussehra rally at Shivaji Park in Mumbai, Uddhav Thackeray rallied his supporters, highlighting the significance of youth activism in addressing the alleged electoral irregularities impacting the fresh electorate. He proclaimed that the saffron identity is a legacy of his party, urging a reformation in the political climate and the prominent display of the saffron flag, echoing the influence of Bal Thackeray in his passionate address.
item.dc:creator: ARYAN SINGH

item.title: Bangladesh furious as Saudi prison list omitted death sentences for 2 citizens
item.dc:creator: VIJAYA SRIVASTAVA

item.title: Kerala man gets Rs 54,500 payout after cruise cancelled without notice
item.description: A family's dream cruise was abruptly canceled without warning, leaving them in distress. The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission in Kerala found both the holiday company and cruise operator at fault. Despite repeated attempts to secure a refund after the cancellation, the complainant was denied compensation. The commission mandated a refund along with additional compensation for the trouble caused, allowing one month for compliance before penalties escalate.
item.dc:creator: SAURABH THAKUR

item.title: Why India slipped in Asian Games standings despite 24 medals as China extend lead
item.description: India achieved 24 medals, achieving five golds on Day 2 of the Asian Para Games 2026. Nishad Kumar and Deepthi Jeevanji led the country with outstanding athletic performances, contributing significantly to the medal tally. Despite this notable success, India's ranking dropped from fourth to sixth due to the gold medal count. China continued to lead the standings with a significant gap over competing nations.
item.dc:creator: HIJAM RAJU SINGH

item.title: 65-year old swimmer killed in shark attack off South African coast; 2 beaches shut
item.description: Tragedy struck at Orient Beach in KuGompo City when 65-year-old open-water swimmer Janine Lochrenberg was fatally attacked by a shark. Despite the desperate efforts of fellow swimmers who rushed to assist her, she suffered life-threatening injuries to her arm and thigh, ultimately succumbing to her wounds. In response, local authorities promptly closed the beach and launched an investigation, as reports indicate a slight rise in shark attacks in recent years.
item.dc:creator: TRISHA MAHAJAN

item.title: Watch: UP MLA Raja Bhaiyya worships 500+ guns on Dusshera
item.description: Raja Bhaiya conducted a Shastra Puja ceremony at his Benti Palace, displaying more than 500 weapons. His twin sons participated alongside block chiefs and hundreds of supporters carrying licensed weapons. This tradition has been observed since ancient times, emphasizing India's cultural heritage. Controversy arose earlier regarding alleged illegal weapons, which Raja Bhaiya's aide denied. Both sons have become increasingly involved in political activities since joining the Jansatta Dal (Loktantrik).
item.dc:creator: RAJEEV MANI

item.title: Trump ‘frustrated and angry’ says Rubio; rejects reports of shift in Ukraine policy
item.description: US secretary of state Marco Rubio reaffirmed the ongoing weapons assistance and intelligence sharing with Ukraine during his visit to India. He expressed frustration regarding the lack of progress in negotiations to end the conflict, emphasizing the situation's urgency. Rubio clarified that the US had not denied Ukraine critical interceptors, which are in high demand globally.
item.dc:creator: PRANJAL PANDEY

item.title: Annamalai backs CJP leaders, questions their continued custody
item.dc:creator: ROHITASHWA RANJAN

item.title: BJP’s delimitation gambit: Will it isolate Cong, puncture opposition’s SIR unity?
item.description: As the government gears up for a new delimitation effort, Congress’s quest for opposition unity faces hurdles. Congress chief Mallikarjun Kharge raised alarms about the government's legislative strategies pertaining to delimitation and reservations for women. With Kiren Rijiju hinting at discussions across various opposition factions that may favor the bills, the scenario presents a complex web of political dynamics.
item.dc:creator: KUNAL VARMA
